title: Whiteboard-of-Thought: Thinking Step-by-Step Across Modalities

model.params_source: paper Appendix 'Experimental details' (temperature 0, max tokens 2048, top p 1, frequency penalty 0.05, presence penalty 0 for direct queries)

task.subset_rule: seeded random 250 (seed 20260907) from the 70,000 examples of task.json
task.approximation: Different 250 items from the paper's unlisted draw and no manual answerability filter (resolution plan); frequency_penalty 0.05 must be passed as an extra API parameter; multiple-choice options removed as in the paper; gold is the target_scores dict; items.label_map maps each of its ten string forms to the digit (runner has no argmax-of-dict facility); item ids are positions in the seeded subset; the paper's frequency_penalty 0.05 is listed in model.params but the runner does not forward it

items.source: github.com/google/BIG-bench, bigbench/benchmark_tasks/mnist_ascii/task.json (57.8 MB, 70,000 examples with fields input = ASCII block and target_scores = {digit: 0/1}; task_prefix 'Please type the digit that you see in the following image: '). Used instead of the tasksource/bigbench parquet mirror because its 'inputs' column carries the loader-appended 'choice: 8 ... choice: 6' lines that the paper removed
items.source_prose: tasksource/bigbench (parquet mirror of google/bigbench; original task JSON github.com/google/BIG-bench bigbench/benchmark_tasks/mnist_ascii/task.json is 57.8 MB)

fields_prose.input: inputs (BIG-bench text: 'Please type the digit that you see in the following image: Q: <ascii art>')
fields_prose.label: targets (list with one digit string)

prompt.user_template:
You are given a task to solve. Make sure to output an answer after "Answer:" without any explanation.

Please type the digit that you see in the following image: 
Q: {task_input}
A:
prompt.source_location: Appendix 'Experimental details' (direct-answer prompt from Yamada et al. 2024) and the ASCII dataset paragraph of the same appendix
prompt.verbatim: full (instruction sentence verbatim; placing it before the task text follows Yamada et al. 2024, the paper does not spell out the concatenation); for the runner the fixed part of the BIG-bench task text (task_prefix and the json-task 'Q:' / 'A:' wrappers, formerly inside the {task_input} slot) is written into the template and only the ASCII block is a placeholder, so the rendered text equals the BIG-bench input without the multiple-choice lines; original template kept in user_template_paper
prompt.user_template_paper:
You are given a task to solve. Make sure to output an answer after "Answer:" without any explanation.

{task_input}

placeholders_prose.task_input: items.input verbatim (BIG-bench 'inputs' field with the ASCII digit), options stripped

output.postprocess: strip, convert to int; conversion failure counts as incorrect (Appendix)

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: share of the 250 items whose integer-converted answer equals the target digit

notes: tasksource/bigbench validation split has the same 13,996 rows as google/bigbench (script-based loader) for mnist_ascii. CoT row (21.6) is an alternative cell with 'Let's think step by step' style prompting not printed. Parse: digit after the last 'Answer:' (greedy prefix), compared as a string with the target digit.
